title: circuitoon-part-spec/1: the input of circuitoon module new
description: A custom part: its name, category, body, its own drawing (art) and pins per side in physical order. Left and right pins run top to bottom, top and bottom pins left to right. A pin is a name, null for a physical gap, or an object.

name.description: What a maker would call it, at most 120 characters.

id.description: Lowercase kebab-case. The module id is this exactly when it starts with "custom-", else "custom-" plus this; left out, "custom-" plus the name made kebab-case.

category.description: A Parts panel group such as Sensors or Displays; default Custom.

source.description: The maker's datasheet and a second source that agrees: URLs, one string separated by spaces or a list.

description.description: Optional: one plain sentence on what the part is, at most 300 characters. The Parts panel searches it (Closest matches) and shows it as the tooltip.

uses.description: Optional: 1 to 8 typical uses, each at most 60 characters and without commas (the New part dialog separates uses with commas) ("battery monitor").

style.description: board (default): a header strip and pin names inside the body. chip: a dark body with names past the pin tips.

w.description: Width in grid units (10 px), 2 to 400. Left out, it fits the pins and labels.

h.description: Height in grid units (10 px), 2 to 400.

color.description: Body colour, #RRGGBB (not used when art is given).

art.description: The part's own drawing, made to look like the real board (see references/art.md in the circuitoon-custom-part skill). Rects in module px on a body of body.w x body.h grid units (10 px each), origin at the body's top left; give body.w and body.h, or art.w and art.h in px (multiples of 10, matching body.w and body.h when both are given). The pins are still placed from pins, over the drawing, and the body must be big enough for them. The renderer adds the dark ink outline to every shape unless outline is false. A shape may stick out of the body by at most 20 px (a jack, a plug). Left out, the part maker draws a generic board or chip. The art of a module from module new copies in whole.

w.description: Body width in px; optional when body.w is given.

h.description: Body height in px; optional when body.h is given.

pinLabels.description: inside: pin names inside the body beside each pin, like silkscreen (boards with a header). tips: past each pin stub's tip (chips). Left out: beside the stub, outside the body.

shapes.description: Drawn in order, first at the back. The largest shape is the body.

radius.description: Corner radius; half the width of a square makes a circle, half the height a pill.

outline.description: false: no ink outline (pads, holes, text plates, fine detail).

label.description: Text centred on the shape (silkscreen, a chip's marking).

labelSize.description: Font size in px; 8 by default.

internal.description: Pins joined inside the part, for example [["GND", "GND 2"]].

side.description: At most 398 pins and gaps a side, so the body stays within 4000 px.

name.description: The silkscreen text. A repeated name is numbered: a second GND becomes "GND 2" with the label "GND".

supply.description: The rails the pin sees or takes: "3V3", "5V", "3V3/5V".

caps.description: Pin capabilities from the chip's datasheet: inputOnly, outputOnly, flash, noPullup, strapping, downloadOnly, note.
